bibl.title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices towards COVID-19 among Chinese residents during the rapid rise period of the COVID-19 outbreak: a quick online cro

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: knowledge, attitudes and practices towards COVID-19 among Chinese residents during the rapid-rise period of the outbreak
span.quote: The knowledge questionnaire consisted of 12 questions regarding the clinical characteristics and prevention of COVID-19.

span.label: what Chinese residents knew, felt and did about COVID-19 while the epidemic was accelerating, and whether knowledge predicted the other two
span.quote: In multiple logistic regression analyses, the COVID-19 knowledge score (OR: 0.75-0.90, P<0.001) was significantly associated with a lower likelihood of negative attitudes and preventive practices towards COVID-2019.

span.label: a 6,910-respondent online KAP survey, reported with the DIRECTION of its own sampling bias on each headline figure
span.quote: Given the significant associations between these demographic variables and KAP towards COVID-19 revealed in this study, we may have overestimated knowledge and rates of preventive practices and underestimated rates of positive attitudes towards COVID-19 of Chinese residents.

span.label: existence
span.quote: The overall correct rate of the knowledge questionnaire was 90%. The majority of the respondents (97.1%) had confidence that China can win the battle against COVID-19. Nearly all of the participants (98.0%) wore masks when going out in recent days.

span.label: high self-reported knowledge, optimism and mask-wearing in a self-selected online sample during an accelerating epidemic
span.quote: The overall correct rate of the knowledge questionnaire was 90%. The majority of the respondents (97.1%) had confidence that China can win the battle against COVID-19. Nearly all of the participants (98.0%) wore masks when going out in recent days.

span.label: self-developed online questionnaire - 12 knowledge items, and attitudes and practices measured with two questions - recruited through the authors' own networks and popular media in Hubei
span.term: self-developed online questionnaire - 12 knowledge items, and attitudes and practices measured with two questions - recruited through the authors' own networks and popular media in Hubei
span.quote: An online sample of Chinese residents was successfully recruited via the authors' networks with residents and popular media in Hubei, China. A self-developed online KAP questionnaire was completed by the participants.

span.label: the proposed pathway is knowledge -> attitude and practice: a higher COVID-19 knowledge score is associated with a LOWER likelihood of negative attitudes and of poor preventive practices, OR 0.75-0.90, P<0.001
span.quote: In multiple logistic regression analyses, the COVID-19 knowledge score (OR: 0.75-0.90, P<0.001) was significantly associated with a lower likelihood of negative attitudes and preventive practices towards COVID-2019.

span.label: knowledge and attitudes act on transmission indirectly through panic, which the paper says can itself complicate prevention
span.quote: Lessons learned from the SARS outbreak in 2003 suggest that knowledge and attitudes towards infectious diseases are associated with level of panic emotion among the population, which can further complicate attempts to prevent the spread of the disease 8 , 9 .

span.label: A SIGNED ERROR TERM, NOT A LIMITATIONS PARAGRAPH. The sample is over-representative of women, the well-educated and mental labourers, and the paper states the consequence per figure: `we may have OVERESTIMATED knowledge and rates of preventive practices and UNDERESTIMATED rates of positive attitudes`
span.quote: Given the significant associations between these demographic variables and KAP towards COVID-19 revealed in this study, we may have overestimated knowledge and rates of preventive practices and underestimated rates of positive attitudes towards COVID-19 of Chinese residents.

span.label: the population the findings apply to is narrowed explicitly - `strictly speaking, our findings can only be generalized to Chinese populations of a relatively high socioeconomic status, particularly women`
span.quote: Considering that educational attainment and occupation are often used as proxy measures of socioeconomic status 22 , strictly speaking, our findings can only be generalized to Chinese populations of a relatively high socioeconomic status, particularly women.

span.label: THE MEASURE IS DECLARED INADEQUATE BY THE PEOPLE WHO USED IT: the assessment of attitudes and practices is `unstandardized and inadequate` and, for want of time, `BOTH WERE MEASURED WITH TWO SIMPLE QUESTIONS ONLY`
span.quote: the second limitation of this study is the unstandardized and inadequate assessment of attitudes and practices towards COVID, which should be developed via focus group discussion and in-depth interview and constructed as multi-dimensional measures. Due to the very limited time for developing the questionnaire, both were measured with two simple questions only.

span.label: and the paper names who is missing and why: vulnerable populations - older adults, rural people - have limited access to internet and online health information, which is the same channel the survey recruited through
span.quote: Due to limited access to internet and online health information resources, vulnerable populations of Chinese society under the COVID-19 epidemic such as older adults and rural people at grass-root level are more likely to have poor knowledge, negative attitudes, and inappropriate preventive practices towards COVID-19.

span.label: community-based national sampling was not feasible during the lockdown, so the survey is an online convenience sample and the paper says so
span.quote: Because it was not feasible to do a community-based national sampling survey during this special period, we decided to collect the data online.

span.label: recruitment ran through the authors' own social networks and local media reposts, which decides who could see the poster at all
span.quote: Relying on the authors' networks with local people living in Hubei, a one-page recruitment poster was posted/reposted to moments and groups of their Wechat (similar to “WhatsApp”) and Weibo (similar to “Twitter”) accounts.

span.label: attitudes rest on two questions and practices on two behaviours, against twelve for knowledge - the three KAP components are not measured at comparable depth
span.quote: Attitudes towards COVID-19 were measured by 2 questions (A1-A2, Table 1 ) about the agreement on the final control of COVID-19 and the confidence in winning the battle against COVID-19.

span.label: the achieved sample is compared against the most recent NATIONAL POPULATION STATISTICS of China, rather than described on its own terms
span.note: eliminates: a self-selected sample being read as a population sample - the comparison is what turns `our respondents` into `over-representative of women, well-educated people, and people engaging in mental labor` · outcome: failed
span.quote: Nevertheless, compared to the most recent national population statistics of China 21 , our sample was obviously over-representative of women, well-educated people, and people engaging in mental labor.

span.label: the DIRECTION of the resulting bias is worked out per outcome, using the associations the study itself measured between the demographic variables and KAP
span.note: eliminates: a caveat that says only `may not generalise` - here the reader is told which numbers are too high and which are too low · outcome: held
span.quote: Given the significant associations between these demographic variables and KAP towards COVID-19 revealed in this study, we may have overestimated knowledge and rates of preventive practices and underestimated rates of positive attitudes towards COVID-19 of Chinese residents.

span.label: whether attitudes and practices were measured adequately
span.note: eliminates: nothing - the assessment is called `unstandardized and inadequate` by the authors, who state that both should have been developed via focus group and interview and built as multi-dimensional measures · outcome: failed
span.quote: the second limitation of this study is the unstandardized and inadequate assessment of attitudes and practices towards COVID, which should be developed via focus group discussion and in-depth interview and constructed as multi-dimensional measures. Due to the very limited time for developing the questionnaire, both were measured with two simple questions only.

span.label: whether the populations most likely to score poorly are in the sample at all
span.note: eliminates: nothing - older adults and rural people have limited internet access, which is the channel the survey recruited through, and the paper says so · outcome: failed
span.quote: Due to limited access to internet and online health information resources, vulnerable populations of Chinese society under the COVID-19 epidemic such as older adults and rural people at grass-root level are more likely to have poor knowledge, negative attitudes, and inappropriate preventive practices towards COVID-19.

span.label: excluding the nine respondents who reported having been infected before analysing the sample
span.note: eliminates: the possibility that people who already had the disease answer knowledge and practice items from experience rather than from public information · outcome: held
span.quote: A total of 6919 participants completed the survey questionnaire.

span.label: backward stepwise selection in the regression models rather than entering all variables
span.note: eliminates: associations that survive only because a correlated demographic is held in the model · outcome: held
span.quote: Factors were selected with a backward stepwise method.

span.label: a yes/no consent item that had to be answered before the questionnaire opened, under ethics approval
span.note: eliminates: participation without informed consent in a survey distributed by social media reposting · outcome: held
span.quote: The Ethics Committee of Wuhan Mental Health Center approved our study protocol and procedures of informed consent before the formal survey.

span.label: knowledge questionnaire
span.quote: The knowledge questionnaire consisted of 12 questions regarding the clinical characteristics and prevention of COVID-19.

span.label: attitudes
span.quote: Assessments on residents' attitudes and practices towards COVID-19 included questions on confidence in winning the battle against COVID-19 and wearing masks when going out in recent days.

span.label: practices
span.quote: Assessments on residents' attitudes and practices towards COVID-19 included questions on confidence in winning the battle against COVID-19 and wearing masks when going out in recent days.

span.label: socioeconomic status
span.quote: Considering that educational attainment and occupation are often used as proxy measures of socioeconomic status 22 , strictly speaking, our findings can only be generalized to Chinese populations of a relatively high socioeconomic status, particularly women.

span.label: KAP theory
span.quote: To guarantee the final success, people's adherence to these control measures are essential, which is largely affected by their knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) towards COVID-19 in accordance with KAP theory 6 , 7 .

span.label: panic emotion
span.quote: Lessons learned from the SARS outbreak in 2003 suggest that knowledge and attitudes towards infectious diseases are associated with level of panic emotion among the population, which can further complicate attempts to prevent the spread of the disease 8 , 9 .

span.label: case fatality rate
span.quote: Empirical clinical data have shown that the overall case fatality rate of COVID-19 is 2.3% in China, much lower than those of SARS (9.5%), MERS (34.4%), and H7N9 (39.0%) 1 - 3 .

span.label: KAP - AS OPERATIONALISED HERE, AND THE THREE ARE NOT EQUAL. Knowledge is 12 items with a correct answer. Attitudes and practices are ONE QUESTION EACH: confidence that China can win, and whether a mask was worn recently. A three-part construct measured 12 : 1 : 1
span.quote: Assessments on residents' attitudes and practices towards COVID-19 included questions on confidence in winning the battle against COVID-19 and wearing masks when going out in recent days.

span.label: the sample - `recruited via the authors' networks with residents and popular media in Hubei`. THE RECRUITMENT CHANNEL IS ALSO THE EXCLUSION CRITERION: it reaches people with internet access, and the paper says the populations most at risk are the ones without it
span.quote: An online sample of Chinese residents was successfully recruited via the authors' networks with residents and popular media in Hubei, China. A self-developed online KAP questionnaire was completed by the participants.

span.label: `most Chinese residents` in the conclusion, WITH ITS QUALIFIER ATTACHED IN THE SAME sentence - `of a relatively high socioeconomic status, in particular women`. The qualifier is inside the claim rather than in a caveat afterwards, which is what makes it survive being quoted
span.quote: Most Chinese residents of a relatively high socioeconomic status, in particular women, are knowledgeable about COVID-19, hold optimistic attitudes, and have appropriate practices towards COVID-19.

span.label: supports → health education programmes as a lever on attitudes and behaviour, on the strength of the knowledge-score association
span.quote: In multiple logistic regression analyses, the COVID-19 knowledge score (OR: 0.75-0.90, P<0.001) was significantly associated with a lower likelihood of negative attitudes and preventive practices towards COVID-2019.

span.label: critiques → generalising KAP findings from an online sample to the Chinese population, which the paper refuses to do for its own results
span.quote: Due to the limited sample representativeness, we must be cautious when generalizing these findings to populations of a low socioeconomic status.

span.label: A SIGNED ERROR TERM: the paper states that it MAY HAVE OVERESTIMATED knowledge and preventive practices and UNDERESTIMATED positive attitudes, deriving the direction from its own measured associations
span.term: A SIGNED ERROR TERM: the paper states that it MAY HAVE OVERESTIMATED knowledge and preventive practices and UNDERESTIMATED positive attitudes, deriving the direction from its own measured associations
span.quote: Given the significant associations between these demographic variables and KAP towards COVID-19 revealed in this study, we may have overestimated knowledge and rates of preventive practices and underestimated rates of positive attitudes towards COVID-19 of Chinese residents.

span.label: THE MEASURE IS DECLARED INADEQUATE BY THE PEOPLE WHO USED IT - attitudes and practices were each measured with TWO SIMPLE QUESTIONS ONLY, for want of time
span.term: THE MEASURE IS DECLARED INADEQUATE BY THE PEOPLE WHO USED IT - attitudes and practices were each measured with TWO SIMPLE QUESTIONS ONLY, for want of time
span.quote: the second limitation of this study is the unstandardized and inadequate assessment of attitudes and practices towards COVID, which should be developed via focus group discussion and in-depth interview and constructed as multi-dimensional measures. Due to the very limited time for developing the questionnaire, both were measured with two simple questions only.

span.label: the overall correct rate on the knowledge questionnaire was 90%, 97.1% had confidence China would win, and 98.0% wore masks when going out
span.term: the overall correct rate on the knowledge questionnaire was 90%, 97.1% had confidence China would win, and 98.0% wore masks when going out
span.quote: The overall correct rate of the knowledge questionnaire was 90%. The majority of the respondents (97.1%) had confidence that China can win the battle against COVID-19. Nearly all of the participants (98.0%) wore masks when going out in recent days.

span.label: a higher knowledge score is associated with a LOWER likelihood of negative attitudes and poor practices, OR 0.75-0.90, P<0.001
span.term: a higher knowledge score is associated with a LOWER likelihood of negative attitudes and poor practices, OR 0.75-0.90, P<0.001
span.quote: In multiple logistic regression analyses, the COVID-19 knowledge score (OR: 0.75-0.90, P<0.001) was significantly associated with a lower likelihood of negative attitudes and preventive practices towards COVID-2019.

span.label: the sample is over-representative of women, the well-educated and mental labourers against national population statistics
span.term: the sample is over-representative of women, the well-educated and mental labourers against national population statistics
span.quote: Nevertheless, compared to the most recent national population statistics of China 21 , our sample was obviously over-representative of women, well-educated people, and people engaging in mental labor.

span.label: THE RECRUITMENT CHANNEL IS ALSO THE EXCLUSION CRITERION: the populations expected to have the poorest knowledge are those with limited internet access, and the survey was online
span.term: THE RECRUITMENT CHANNEL IS ALSO THE EXCLUSION CRITERION: the populations expected to have the poorest knowledge are those with limited internet access, and the survey was online
span.quote: Due to limited access to internet and online health information resources, vulnerable populations of Chinese society under the COVID-19 epidemic such as older adults and rural people at grass-root level are more likely to have poor knowledge, negative attitudes, and inappropriate preventive practices towards COVID-19.

span.label: COVID-19's case fatality rate in China was far below SARS, MERS and H7N9, which is the comparison the paper opens with
span.quote: Empirical clinical data have shown that the overall case fatality rate of COVID-19 is 2.3% in China, much lower than those of SARS (9.5%), MERS (34.4%), and H7N9 (39.0%) 1 - 3 .

span.label: the achieved sample is markedly more educated and more female than the population it is meant to describe
span.quote: Among this final sample, the average age was 33.0 years (standard deviation [SD]: 10.7, range: 16-87), 4542 (65.7%) were women, 4387 (63.5%) held a bachelor's degree or above, 3881 (56.2%) engaged in mental labor, and 3810 (55.1%) were Hubei residents.

span.label: the knowledge instrument reached acceptable internal consistency, which the paper states with the coefficient
span.quote: The Cronbach's alpha coefficient of the knowledge questionnaire was 0.71 in our sample, indicating acceptable internal consistency 12 .

span.label: 12 questions regarding the clinical characteristics and prevention of COVID-19
span.quote: The knowledge questionnaire consisted of 12 questions regarding the clinical characteristics and prevention of COVID-19.

span.label: the knowledge instrument's construction - twelve items split across clinical presentation, transmission, and prevention, scored 0 to 12
span.quote: The questionnaire had 12 questions (Table 1 ): 4 regarding clinical presentations (K1-K4), 3 regarding transmission routes (K5-K7), and 5 regarding prevention and control (K8-K12) of COVID-19.

span.label: survey completers, of whom 65.7% women, 63.5% with a bachelor degree or above, 56.2% in mental labour
span.quote: Among the survey completers (n=6910), 65.7% were women, 63.5% held a bachelor degree or above, and 56.2% engaged in mental labor.

span.label: items in the knowledge questionnaire - against one question each for attitudes and for practices
span.quote: The knowledge questionnaire consisted of 12 questions regarding the clinical characteristics and prevention of COVID-19.

span.label: per cent overall correct rate on the knowledge questionnaire
span.quote: The overall correct rate of the knowledge questionnaire was 90%. The majority of the respondents (97.1%) had confidence that China can win the battle against COVID-19. Nearly all of the participants (98.0%) wore masks when going out in recent days.

span.label: case fatality of COVID-19 against SARS, MERS and H7N9
span.quote: Empirical clinical data have shown that the overall case fatality rate of COVID-19 is 2.3% in China, much lower than those of SARS (9.5%), MERS (34.4%), and H7N9 (39.0%) 1 - 3 .

span.label: the share of Chinese COVID-19 patients progressing to the severe stage
span.quote: In China, 18.5% of the patients with COVID-19 develop to the severe stage, which is characterized by acute respiratory distress syndrome, septic shock, difficult-to-tackle metabolic acidosis, and bleeding and coagulation dysfunction 1 , 2 .

span.label: the analysed sample and its demographic composition
span.quote: Among this final sample, the average age was 33.0 years (standard deviation [SD]: 10.7, range: 16-87), 4542 (65.7%) were women, 4387 (63.5%) held a bachelor's degree or above, 3881 (56.2%) engaged in mental labor, and 3810 (55.1%) were Hubei residents.

span.label: logistic regression
span.quote: In multiple logistic regression analyses, the COVID-19 knowledge score (OR: 0.75-0.90, P<0.001) was significantly associated with a lower likelihood of negative attitudes and preventive practices towards COVID-2019.

span.label: OR
span.quote: In multiple logistic regression analyses, the COVID-19 knowledge score (OR: 0.75-0.90, P<0.001) was significantly associated with a lower likelihood of negative attitudes and preventive practices towards COVID-2019.

span.label: the modelling strategy: linear regression for knowledge score, logistic for attitudes and practices, reported as beta and odds ratios with confidence intervals
span.quote: Multivariable linear regression analysis using all of the demographic variables as independent variables and knowledge score as the outcome variable was conducted to identify factors associated with knowledge.

span.label: socioeconomic status
span.quote: Considering that educational attainment and occupation are often used as proxy measures of socioeconomic status 22 , strictly speaking, our findings can only be generalized to Chinese populations of a relatively high socioeconomic status, particularly women.

span.label: knowledge score
span.quote: In multiple logistic regression analyses, the COVID-19 knowledge score (OR: 0.75-0.90, P<0.001) was significantly associated with a lower likelihood of negative attitudes and preventive practices towards COVID-2019.

span.label: the demographic variables entered as predictors, including place of residence as Hubei against other provinces
span.quote: Demographic variables included age, gender, marital status, education, occupation, and place of current residence (Hubei vs. other provinces of China).

p.note: The full text of this article is not redistributable, so it is not included here. Every tag above carries the exact sentence it was made from, quoted under fair quotation. The article itself is at https://doi.org/10.7150/ijbs.45221.
